acceptance.spec.ts
---BINE2E---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

=== V14__notes.sql ===
-- Notes: free-text notes written on a target (a project for now; target_type/target_id keep it
-- open to other targets later). Each note carries its text and the instant it was written, stored
-- as an ISO-8601 string so the value surfaced is exactly what was stored and newest-first is a
-- simple descending sort. GENERATED BY DEFAULT (not ALWAYS) so the /__test__ seed path can insert
-- explicit fixture ids.
CREATE TABLE notes (
    id          BIGINT        GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    target_type VARCHAR(32)   NOT NULL,
    target_id   BIGINT        NOT NULL,
    note_text   VARCHAR(4000) NOT NULL,
    noted_at    VARCHAR(40)   NOT NULL
);
=== projects notes GET yml ===
# GET /api/projects/{projectId}/notes -> list every note on one project, newest first (ProjectNotesGet.service).
service:
  class: net.officefloor.hq.app.ProjectNotesGet

The test passes. Here's what I implemented for **"add notes to invoices too"**:

**The change was small because notes were already built generic** — the `notes` table (`target_type`/`target_id`, Flyway V14), the `POST /api/notes` endpoint, and the `/__test__` seed path all already support any target. So no schema migration or seed change was needed; "invoice" is just a second target alongside "project".

What I added (all new, additive files):

**Server (OfficeFloor):**
- `rest/api/invoices/{id}/notes.GET.yml` — wires the new endpoint
- `InvoiceNotesGet.java` — `GET /api/invoices/{id}/notes`, reads notes with `target_type = "invoice"`, newest first, mirroring `ProjectNotesGet`

**Front-end (one slot filling the existing `InvoiceDetail` region — CLAUDE.md rule 3, nothing existing edited except additive query helpers):**
- `features/notes/queries.ts` — added `invoiceNotesKey`/`fetchInvoiceNotes` (key nested under `['invoices', id, 'notes']`)
- `features/notes/InvoiceNotesTable.tsx` — queries for itself, renders `note-row-*` / `note-text` / `note-at`
- `features/notes/InvoiceNoteForm.tsx` — reuses the shared `createNote` mutation with an `invoice` target, invalidates the invoice-notes key
- `features/notes/invoice-notes.slot.tsx` — fills `InvoiceDetail` with the `invoice-notes` panel

All the `data-testid` anchors the spec reads (`invoice-notes`, `note-row-1`, `note-text`, `note-form-text`, `note-form-submit`) match, the frontend typechecks, and the Playwright test passes.
